text: SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER. Blood pressure is written as two numbers. The top number (systolic) is the pressure when the heart beats; the bottom number (diastolic) is the pressure when the heart rests between beats. One reading can vary, so decisions are based on several readings.

SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER. High blood pressure is usually confirmed with repeated measurements on different days, sometimes with home or ambulatory monitoring. The exact thresholds depend on the guideline a clinician follows.
SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER. Common risk factors for high blood pressure include a high-salt diet, low physical activity, excess weight, heavy alcohol use, family history and older age.

SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER. Over many years, untreated high blood pressure can damage blood vessels and raise the risk of heart attack, stroke and kidney disease. It often causes no symptoms, which is why regular checks matter.

SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER. Lifestyle changes that can lower blood pressure include eating less salt, following a diet rich in vegetables and fruit, being physically active most days, limiting alcohol and keeping a healthy weight.
SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER. Blood pressure medicines work in different ways. Normal readings while taking a medicine usually mean it is working; any change or stop should be discussed with a clinician.
